historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 2.85% diverges >30% from EPS 5yr CAGR 8.65%: equity is held down by ~EUR0.8bn/yr dividends plus EUR2.0bn of buybacks FY2022-26; EPS recovered from the 2022 input-cost trough. Revenue 3yr CAGR is negative (-2.9%) because of the Consumer Brands portfolio pruning (~EUR1bn of divested/discontinued sales) and FX. Neither series is used mechanically; the driver path anchors to organic guidance (1.5-3.5% FY2026; 3-4% mid-term ambition).
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF equals reported FCF (SBC zero, interest income not deducted), so the FCF CAGRs are on a consistent series. The 3yr FCF CAGR (41%) starts at the 2022 trough (EUR654m, inventory build + raw-material spike) and the 5yr (-4.9%) ends on a NWC-depressed 2025 - both endpoints are distorted; FY2019-FY2025 owner FCF averaged ~EUR2.1bn.

scenario_narratives.base: Henkel delivers its guidance and the bottom of its mid-term ambition: Adhesive Technologies grows ~3-4% organically on Mobility & Electronics and packaging, Consumer Brands ~1-3% with Hair offsetting Laundry & Home Care private-label pressure in Europe, FX costs ~3.5% of reported sales in 2026 then is neutral. Reported EBITDA margin edges from 17.3% to ~18.3% (adjusted EBIT ~16%) as the Consumer Brands merger savings complete, but recurring restructuring keeps reported margins below adjusted. Acquisitions (ATP, NYM, Olaplex, Stahl) earn roughly their cost of capital.
scenario_narratives.bull: The portfolio upgrade works: Stahl and ATP lift Adhesive Technologies toward high-teens margins and 4-5% organic growth on electronics/EV and specialty coatings, Hair (Olaplex, Not Your Mother's, Schwarzkopf) becomes a premium growth engine, and Consumer Brands holds mid-teens margins against P&G/Unilever. Group organic growth reaches the top of the 3-4% ambition, reported EBITDA climbs to 19.5% as restructuring tails off, and capex stays lean.
scenario_narratives.bear: Consumer Brands proves sub-scale: retail consolidation and private label erode Laundry & Home Care pricing in Europe, Olaplex keeps shrinking, and the European auto slump (~20% of Adhesive sales) persists. Raw-material inflation from the Middle East tensions and a weak dollar squeeze margins; reported EBITDA slides to 16% and organic growth stalls at ~1.5% nominal, while integrating four acquisitions at once raises capex and restructuring.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Henkel is a mature, low-growth, high-quality EUR compounder: the value is a ~10% owner-FCF margin on ~EUR20bn of sales, growing roughly with nominal GDP. The valuation is terminal-heavy and capped at 15x terminal FCF (Gordon at 7%/2% would be ~20x), so it does not rely on multiple expansion. The SBC band collapses (SBC-zero market). Largest judgment: acquisitions valued at cost.
key_risks_to_valuation: Acquisitions valued at purchase price: ~EUR5.3bn deployed in 2026 (ATP, NYM, Olaplex, Stahl); a 30% overpayment would be ~EUR4/share
FX translation: 62% of sales outside Europe; a weaker USD lowers EUR flows
Consumer Brands private-label erosion in Europe
Terminal value ~55-60% of EV and bound by the 15x cap in base/bull

Share count: 404.85M at Jun-2026 treasury count; parser history before FY2025 used a constant 434.278M (gross shares less older treasury) and back-solved FY2022-24 counts, which affects historical per-share series but not this valuation

inputs.share_count_basis: Ordinary + preferred shares outstanding at 2026-06-30: 437.958M issued (178.163M ordinary + 259.796M preferred) less treasury 6.386M ordinary and 26.722M preferred (H1-2026 report, treasury-share note) = 404.85M. Both classes counted because they have equal claims on earnings (preferred carry only a EUR0.02 dividend preference); value per share applies to HEN3 and HEN alike. Supersedes the parser's FY2025 406.788M (same method, Dec-2025 treasury count); FY2022-24 back-solved counts not used. No dilutive securities (LTI is cash-settled). Held FLAT: buyback programme (~EUR1bn, May-2025 to Mar-2026) is complete and none is authorised-and-running.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report statement of changes in equity: equity-settled share-based payments 0 in FY2025 (18 in FY2024); Henkel's LTI is predominantly cash-settled and its cost already sits in operating cash flow, so it is charged in the flows. Equity-award taxes 0. SBC-zero market treatment: house and street coincide.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:35:19Z (Yahoo regularMarketTime, Xetra regular session; Friday close carried to Sunday valuation date)
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR build: 10y Bund ~2.7%, ERP 5.5%, beta ~0.8 (defensive consumer/industrial) -> cost of equity ~7.1%; after-tax cost of single-A debt ~2.8% at <10% of capital -> WACC 7.0%. Same WACC in every scenario: risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (adaptation f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease payments (principal + interest, 'Redemption of lease liabilities' ~EUR69m per half incl. lease interest, H1-2026 cash flow statement) charged at 0.7% of revenue inside EBIT; D&A path (2.8%) is ex right-of-use depreciation (~EUR130m of FY2025's EUR678m); lease liabilities (EUR666m at 2025-12-31) EXCLUDED from net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are ~EUR86m of equity (0.3%), profit share immaterial; not deducted. Immaterial either way.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company: adhesives + consumer brands) per dcf-methods routing row 'non-US consumer/industrial', with owner-fcf-adaptations applied (EUR WACC, lease treatment B, SBC-zero, risk charged once). First valuation of this ticker - no prior DCF or memory entry. FCF basis is OCF - capex (parser definition), not Henkel's own 'free cash flow' (EUR1,850m FY2025). FY2025 owner FCF 1,842 was depressed by a NWC build (NWC 3.8% of sales vs 3.0%); FY2023/FY2024 were 2,647/2,494. Interest income (EUR96m FY2025) NOT deducted: the group moved from EUR109m net financial position at Dec-2025 to EUR1,855m net debt at Jun-2026, so there is no material cash pile being double-counted. Net debt = Henkel's net financial position at 2026-06-30 (borrowings 6,091 less cash 3,987 and readily monetisable securities/derivatives 249). M&A treatment: the flows are the FY2025 perimeter only (FY2026 growth path is organic + FX, excluding acquisition contributions). ATP Adhesive Systems (EUR903m) and Not Your Mother's (EUR786m), paid in cash in H1-2026 and therefore inside the June net debt, are added back at purchase price in the equity bridge (acquisitions valued at cost, NPV-neutral). OLAPLEX (EUR1,525m paid 2026-07-07) and Stahl (EUR2.1bn agreed 2026-02-04, pending) post-date the balance sheet: cash out and asset in at cost net to zero, so neither is in the bridge. If these deals destroy value (Olaplex's revenue was shrinking before the deal) the at-cost assumption overstates IV by the overpayment. H1-2026 owner FCF (~EUR430m: OCF 862 - capex 316 - leases ~70 - ~45 interest earned) is already in the June cash AND inside the full-year FY2026 projection, so it is deducted once in the bridge. Buybacks: EUR856m FY2025 and EUR144m H1-2026 completed the ~EUR1bn programme; the flat count is a convention, not a funded commitment, but there is no SBC dilution to offset.

base.growth_rates_rationale: FY2026: organic guidance midpoint 2.5% less ~3.5% FX translation (H1 FX effect -3.9%), acquisitions excluded (valued at cost in the bridge). FY2027-30 at the bottom of the 3-4% mid-term organic ambition, fading to 2.5% nominal.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Reported (post-restructuring) EBITDA: 17.0% FY2025, 17.3% H1-2026. Adjusted EBIT guidance 14.5-16.0% FY2026 and ~16% mid-term implies ~19.5% adjusted EBITDA; reported runs ~1-1.5pp below because restructuring is recurring at Henkel. Base reaches 18.3%.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes paid 651 on EBIT ~2,816 FY2025 (23%); group effective rate ~25%. 24.5% on pre-interest EBIT.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer: NWC ~3-4% of sales, so growth consumes cash; capture -4% of the revenue change.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): consumer private-label pressure, European auto weakness and simultaneous integration of ~EUR5.3bn of debt-funded acquisitions in one year are live, though the single-A balance sheet rules out solvency risk. Base 55%: guidance was raised twice in 2026 and H1 landed in the upper half of every range. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs both the M&A portfolio upgrade and a Consumer Brands share recovery to come good together.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
